passage: At 3 o'clock the enemy's line of battle left the woods in our front
note: Webb: assault begins at 3 o'clock. Hunt (R028 p.239) 'About 3 p. m.'. Hour carried as a range (Peyton 14:30; A. Hays 16:30; Lang nearly 16:00 p.632). Distance: Lee p.318 'the ground was undulating and generally open for about three-quarters of a mile' describes the open ground in front of the Federal position in his general account, not the Jul 3 advance distance specifically; 'nearly one mile' and 'closes to 2,200 ft (68%)' are not in the OR. Participating divisions (Pickett, Pettigrew, Trimble) supported by Lee p.320.

passage: we had a raking fire through all three of these lines
note: McGilvery's guns trained obliquely right gave a raking fire through the three advancing lines (supports McGilvery fire on the Confederate right, not named 'Pickett'). passage: Our fire was poured into their flank with terrible effect
note: Sawyer, 8th Ohio: front changed to the left flank of the advancing column, 'about 200' prisoners and 3 stands of colours. Supported: 8th Ohio flank fire on the advance, hour 'after about 2 p.m. ... advance'. Not in the OR text read: '160 men', Brockenbrough fleeing into Trimble, Davis's brigade, '1,600 rounds'.

passage: I am badly wounded, though I trust not seriously.
note: Hancock's note to Meade (Jul 3, Twelfth Corps Hospital dateline follows): 'I was shot with a tenpenny nail' and 'I did not leave the field till the victory was entirely secured'. Supports Hancock wounded and leaving after the repulse; does NOT support saddle pommel or inner right thigh, nor that he refused evacuation during the charge (he states he left after victory). Time and place remain a gap.
